title: Lord, What Was Man, When Made at First
description: Lord, What Was Man, When Made at First in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 8, part 4, headed “Second Part. L. M. Adam and Christ, lords of the old and the new creation”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, what was man, when made at first, A-dam the off-spring of the dust, That thou shouldst set him and his race But just be-low an an-gel's place?

lines: Lord, what was man, when made at first,
Adam the offspring of the dust,
That thou shouldst set him and his race
But just below an angel's place?
That thou shouldst raise his nature so
And make him lord of all below;
Make every beast and bird submit,
And lay the fishes at his feet?
But O, what brighter glories wait
To crown the second Adam's state!
What honours shall thy Son adorn
Who condescended to be born!
See him below his angels made,
See him in dust amongst the dead,
To save a ruin'd world from sin;
But he shall reign with power divine.
The world to come, redeem'd from all
The miseries that attend the fall,
New made, and glorious, shall submit
At our exalted Saviour's feet.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
